s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive skin lesions with pruritic erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques localized to the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Histopathologic examination revealed multiple milia in the superficial dermis
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive skin lesions with pruritic erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques localized to the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Histopathologic examination revealed multiple milia in the superficial dermis
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

raw.rationale: The presence of dermoepidermal separation and milia on histopathologic examination, along with the identification of a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, strongly supports the diagnosis of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
rejected.why: The presence of dermoepidermal separation and milia, as well as the COL7A1 variant, are more characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa than Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex.

rejected.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
rejected.why: The lack of mucous membrane involvement and the specific histopathologic findings are not typical of Bullous Pemphigoid.

rejected.label: Lichen Planus
rejected.why: The presence of dermoepidermal separation and milia are not characteristic of Lichen Planus, which typically presents with a distinct set of clinical and histopathologic features.

rejected.label: Prurigo Nodularis
rejected.why: The histopathologic findings and genetic testing results do not support a diagnosis of Prurigo Nodularis, which is a condition characterized by intense pruritus and nodular lesions without a clear genetic basis.
